stem: A hospital is redesigning its antimicrobial stewardship program. Which role assignment best reflects current CDC guidance?

options.A: Use physician-pharmacist stewardship leadership, with trained pharmacy expertise participating in program management and interventions such as prospective audit and feedback or preauthorization.
options.B: Limit the pharmacist to medication dispensing and exclude pharmacy expertise from antimicrobial-use decisions.
options.C: Assign stewardship responsibility to nursing alone and avoid collaboration with physicians or pharmacists so accountability remains with one discipline.
options.D: Use pharmacy expertise only after an antimicrobial course is complete because stewardship interventions should not influence active prescribing.

rationale: A is correct. CDC's current Hospital Core Elements identify accountability and pharmacy expertise as core stewardship components and note that many effective programs are co-led by a physician and pharmacist. CDC also recommends active stewardship interventions such as prospective audit and feedback or preauthorization. Current 2026 multi-society guidance likewise describes stewardship as multidisciplinary and emphasizes clinical infectious-diseases, pharmacology, microbiology, quality-improvement, communication, and program-evaluation skills. B and D improperly reduce the pharmacist to a dispensing role. C conflicts with the collaborative program structure recommended by CDC.
educational_objective: Recognize antimicrobial stewardship as a multidisciplinary care-management function in which trained pharmacy expertise participates in program leadership, antimicrobial review, and active prescribing interventions rather than being limited to medication dispensing.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC); SHEA/SIDP/PIDS/IDSA
source_document_title: Core Elements of Hospital Antibiotic Stewardship Programs; Priorities for Hospital Core Element Implementation; Guidance for the Knowledge and Skills Required for Antimicrobial Stewardship Leaders
source_version_date: CDC Hospital Core Elements page dated September 15, 2025; CDC implementation priorities current 2026; multi-society guidance published May 11, 2026; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: CDC Hospital Core Elements — Accountability/Pharmacy Expertise: appoint a leader or co-leaders such as a physician and pharmacist responsible for program management and outcomes; Action: implement prospective audit and feedback or preauthorization. CDC Priorities — Accountability: co-leadership by physician and pharmacist is an effective model; Pharmacy/Stewardship Expertise: leaders should have ID specialty, certificate, or other stewardship training. 2026 SHEA/SIDP/PIDS/IDSA Guidance — Introduction: antimicrobial stewardship is coordinated, multidisciplinary work requiring clinical ID, pharmacology, microbiology, quality-improvement, communication, and measurement skills.
source_claim_supported: Current stewardship guidance supports active physician-pharmacist leadership and trained pharmacy participation in antimicrobial-use interventions and program management rather than a dispensing-only role.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members and participate in quality-improvement systems to promote safe client care.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — multidisciplinary antimicrobial stewardship
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source's generic pharmacist-role definition into a current program-design decision. The final item uses CDC's explicit physician-pharmacist accountability/pharmacy-expertise elements and current 2026 multidisciplinary stewardship guidance, avoiding unsupported claims that every pharmacist independently sets doses or treatment plans.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against CDC's current Hospital Core Elements/Priorities and the May 2026 multi-society stewardship-leader guidance.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A combines explicit CDC accountability, pharmacy-expertise, and Action elements. B and D remove pharmacy expertise from active stewardship. C rejects the multidisciplinary leadership model.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; pharmacist expertise participates in leadership and active stewardship interventions.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; CDC identifies pharmacy expertise as a core element.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; stewardship is multidisciplinary rather than nursing-only.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; stewardship interventions are intended to improve active antimicrobial prescribing.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The item does not claim one mandatory staffing model for every hospital; it asks which assignment best reflects current guidance, making A uniquely defensible.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe program-role assignments at similar scope.
audit_findings.blueprint: Team collaboration and quality-improvement program participation fit Management of Care.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked whether co-leadership is absolutely mandatory for every hospital; CDC notes resource-sensitive exceptions. The final wording says 'best reflects' and avoids a universal staffing mandate while preserving the explicit role of trained pharmacy expertise. No second answer remained.
